They are screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1, top right): 7 frozen indicators are confirmed on held-out, and the pooled partial Spearman of the OPEN index is +0.069. Separately (lower arrow, bypassing the indicators), a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent concept frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2, bottom right). It gives d<sub>0</sub> = 0.322 for retained-frontier relatedness, and the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL because persistence is confounded with volume.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n  <figure>\n    <img src=\"figures/fig_case_study_v0.png\" alt=\"Three panels. Left: step lines of off-home fields entered and retained over eight years since onset; GPU rises to 11 entered and 8 retained, VAWT to 6 entered and 4 retained. Middle: GPU's early topic ego network with 34 topics in 8 colour-coded communities. Right: VAWT's network with 12 topics in one Engineering community.\" loading=\"lazy\" width=\"1300\" height=\"558\">\n    <figcaption>Figure 4 of the paper. Illustrative matched case-study pair (pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset t<sub>0</sub>=2008, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; t<sub>0</sub>=2009, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+8; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field. GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30). VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness–breadth association and is not evidence for it. class=\"q\">How often does openness point the wrong way for a single concept?</p>\n    <h3 id=\"h-ms\">Misses among the most and least open concepts</h3>\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\"><table id=\"ms-table\"><caption class=\"sr\">Misses by body</caption></table></div>\n    <div class=\"controls\" style=\"margin-top:10px\">\n      <button class=\"plain\" type=\"button\" id=\"ms-show-high\">Show top-fifth misses in the browser</button>\n      <button class=\"plain\" type=\"button\" id=\"ms-show-low\">Show bottom-fifth misses in the browser</button>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"t-miss\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>\n  <ul class=\"prose limits\">\n    <li><strong>Not a forecasting tool.</strong> OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [−0.003, +0.008]). The association is modest.</li>\n    <li><strong>Not confirmatory for most bodies.</strong> Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks. Only the 2015–17 cohort was never used before.</li>\n    <li><strong>Not temporal churn.</strong> The within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component (excess NOVCHURN +0.008 [−0.02, +0.03] against raw +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]). The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability of about 0.01–0.05, so temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.</li>\n    <li><strong>Not a within-concept mechanism.</strong> The closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields (−0.079 [−0.146, −0.013]).</li>\n    <li><strong>Home-only signal is marginal.</strong> On the fresh cohort the DerSimonian–Laird pool includes zero (+0.083 [−0.007, +0.173]); about half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is mechanical coupling with the outcome.</li>\n    <li><strong>Retained frontier is PARTIAL.</strong> The volume-matched contrast is null, the coefficient reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity, and persistence and volume remain confounded.</li>\n    <li><strong>Not causal.</strong> Early openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.</li>\n    <li><strong>Vocabulary bias.</strong> The legacy concept vocabulary is survivor-selected; the vocabulary-free Frame N is small (636 concepts) with pre-unseal power of 0.47.</li>\n  </ul>\n</div>\n</section>\n</main>\n\n<footer id=\"sources\" aria-labelledby=\"h-src\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-src\">Sources, provenance and glossary</h2>\n  <div class=\"links\">\n    <a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_e4QYTG8fEPNh/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n    <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_e4QYTG8fEPNh/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n    <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_e4QYTG8fEPNh\">Code repository</a>\n  </div>\n  <h3>Where each view's data comes from</h3>\n  <ul class=\"prose small\" id=\"prov-list\">\n    <li><strong>Headline forest:</strong> evaluation 4, <code>results/evidence_synthesis.json</code> (per-body PSP, CIs, placebo percentiles, DerSimonian–Laird pools).</li>\n    <li><strong>Stepper, concept browser, fifths view, calculator, misses:</strong> experiment 16, <code>full_method_out.json</code> (7,748 concepts; tip.hidden = false; tipOwner = target;\n  const r = target.getBoundingClientRect(), tr = tip.getBoundingClientRect();\n  let x = r.left + window.scrollX + r.width / 2 - tr.width / 2;\n  x = Math.max(8 + window.scrollX, Math.min(x, window.scrollX + document.documentElement.clientWidth - tr.width - 8));\n  let y = r.top + window.scrollY - tr.height - 8;\n  if (y < window.scrollY + 4) y = r.bottom + window.scrollY + 8;\n  tip.style.left = x + \"px\"; g.setAttribute(\"aria-label\", label); g.classList.add(\"mark\");\n  const on = () => showTip(html, g);\n  g.addEventListener(\"mouseenter\", on); g.addEventListener(\"focus\", on); g.addEventListener(\"click\", e => { e.stopPropagation(); on(); });\n  g.addEventListener(\"mouseleave\", () => { if (tipOwner === g) hideTip(); });\n  g.addEventListener(\"blur\", () => { if (tipOwner === g) hideTip(); });\n}\ndocument.addEventListener(\"click\", () => { if (tipOwner && tipOwner.classList && tipOwner.classList.contains(\"mark\")) hideTip(); });\n\n/* ---------- scales ---------- */\nfunction niceTicks(lo, hi, n){\n  const span = hi - lo, raw = span / Math.max(1, n), mag = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(raw)));\n  const step = [1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10].map(m => m * mag).find(s => span / s <= n) || 10 * mag;\n  const out = []; File: /tmp/claude-10001/-ai-inventor-aii-data-runs-run-e4QYTG8fEPNh-4-gen-paper-repo--4-assemble-paper-paper/eef674d4-f497-4b2f-9e18-c4554ab09a90/scratchpad/check.py

```
import sys, json, shutil
from pathlib import Path
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

PAGE = "file:///ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_e4QYTG8fEPNh/4_gen_paper_repo/_4_assemble_paper/paper/interactive.html"
SHOTS = Path(__file__).parent / "shots"
SHOTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
exe = shutil.which("chromium-headless-shell")

OVERLAP_JS = """
() => {
  const res = [];
  document.querySelectorAll('.chart svg').forEach((svg, si) => {
    const ts = Array.from(svg.querySelectorAll('text')).map(t => ({t: t.textContent, b: t.getBoundingClientRect()}));
    for (let i = 0; i < ts.length; i++) for (let j = i + 1; j < ts.length; j++) {
      const a = ts[i].b, b = ts[j].b;
      if (a.width === 0 || b.width === 0) continue;
      const ox = Math.min(a.right, b.right) - Math.max(a.left, b.left), oy = Math.min(a.bottom, b.bottom) - Math.max(a.top, b.top);
      if (ox > 1 && oy > 1) res.push([svg.closest('.chart').id, ts[i].t, ts[j].t]);
    }
    // text outside svg horizontally
    const sb = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
    ts.forEach(x => { if (x.b.width && (x.b.left < sb.left - 1 || x.b.right > sb.right + 1)) res.push([svg.closest('.chart').id, 'CLIPPED', x.t]); });
  });
  return res;
}
"""


def run(width, tag, actions=True):
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        b = p.chromium.launch(executable_path=exe)
        ctx = b.new_context(viewport={"width": width, "height": 900}, has_touch=(width < 500))
        pg = ctx.new_page()
        msgs = []
        pg.on("console", lambda m: msgs.append(f"{m.type}: {m.text}"))
        pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: msgs.append(f"PAGEERROR: {e}"))
        pg.on("requestfailed", lambda r: msgs.append(f"REQFAIL: {r.url}"))
        pg.goto(PAGE)
        pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
        info = pg.evaluate("() => ({sw: document.documentElement.scrollWidth, cw: document.documentElement.clientWidth, svgs: document.querySelectorAll('svg').length, imgs: document.querySelectorAll('img').length})")
        print(tag, info)
        print(tag, "overlaps", json.dumps(pg.evaluate(OVERLAP_JS))[:3000])
        pg.screenshot(path=str(SHOTS / f"{tag}_full.png"), full_page=True)
        for sid in ["finding", "how", "v-browser", "v-quint", "v-entry", "v-strata", "v-calc", "v-topk", "v-robust", "v-conf", "v-miss", "sources"]:
            loc = pg.locator("#" + sid)
            loc.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
            loc.screenshot(path=str(SHOTS / f"{tag}_{sid}.png"))
        if actions:
            # headline controls
            pg.click("#hd-rung button[data-v=R0]"); pg.click("#hd-feature button[data-v=NOVCHURN_home]")
            print("T headline:", pg.inner_text("#t-headline"))
            pg.locator("#v-headline").screenshot(path=str(SHOTS / f"{tag}_headline_nov_r0.png"))
            pg.click("#hd-rung button[data-v=R2]"); pg.click("#hd-feature button[data-v=OPEN_home]")
            print("T headline:", pg.inner_text("#t-headline"))
            # hover mark
            m = pg.locator("#c-headline .mark").first
            m.hover(); pg.wait_for_timeout(100)
            print("tip:", pg.inner_text("#tip"), pg.is_visible("#tip"))
            # stepper
            for i in range(6):
                print("step", i, pg.inner_text("#st-live"), "| prev disabled", pg.is_disabled("#st-prev"), "next disabled", pg.is_disabled("#st-next"))
                pg.locator("#stepper").screenshot(path=str(SHOTS / f"{tag}_step{i}.png"))
                if i < 5:
                    pg.click("#st-next")
            pg.locator("#stage-list button").nth(2).click()
            pg.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")
            print("after arrow:", pg.inner_text("#st-live"))
            # term click persists
            t = pg.locator("button.term").first
            t.click(); pg.wait_for_timeout(150)
            print("term visible after click:", pg.is_visible("#tip"), pg.inner_text("#tip")[:60])
            pg.mouse.click(5, 5); pg.wait_for_timeout(100)
            print("term visible after outside click:", pg.is_visible("#tip"))
            # browser
            pg.fill("#br-q", "CRISPR"); pg.wait_for_timeout(100)
            print("count:", pg.inner_text("#br-count"))
            pg.locator("#br-list button").first.click()
            print("detail:", pg.inner_text("#br-detail")[:300].replace("\n", " | "))
            print("T browser:", pg.inner_text("#t-browser"))
            pg.fill("#br-q", "")
            pg.select_option("#br-filter", "miss-high")
            print("count miss:", pg.inner_text("#br-count"))
            pg.select_option("#br-filter", "all"); pg.select_option("#br-sort", "surprise-desc"); pg.select_option("#br-body", "COH1517")
            print("count coh:", pg.inner_text("#br-count"))
            pg.locator("#v-browser").screenshot(path=str(SHOTS / f"{tag}_browser2.png"))
            # quint
            for v in ["DEV", "COH1517"]:
                pg.click(f"#qu-body button[data-v={v}]")
                print("T quint:", pg.inner_text("#t-quint"))
            # entry units
            pg.locator("#en-units input[data-u=MATHDEC]").uncheck()
            print("T entry:", pg.inner_text("#t-entry"))
            # strata
            pg.select_option("#sb-unit", "SOC")
            pg.check("#sb-flip")
            print("T strata:", pg.inner_text("#t-strata"))
            pg.locator("#v-strata").screenshot(path=str(SHOTS / f"{tag}_strata2.png"))
            # topk
            pg.fill("#tk-k", "1"); pg.dispatch_event("#tk-k", "input")
            print("T topk:", pg.inner_text("#t-topk"))
            # calc
            print("calc:", pg.inner_text("#calc-out"))
            pg.fill("#cs-0", "0.1"); pg.dispatch_event("#cs-0", "input")
            print("calc edited:", pg.inner_text("#calc-out"))
            pg.click("#calc-reset")
            # robust tabs
            for v in ["dose", "robust", "fail"]:
                pg.click(f"#rb-tabs button[data-v={v}]")
                print("T robust:", pg.inner_text("#t-robust"))
            pg.select_option("#cf-body", "COH1517")
            print("T conf:", pg.inner_text("#t-conf"))
            print("T miss:", pg.inner_text("#t-miss"))
            pg.click("#ms-show-low")
            print("count after miss button:", pg.inner_text("#br-count"))
            info = pg.evaluate("() => ({sw: document.documentElement.scrollWidth, cw: document.documentElement.clientWidth})")
            print(tag, "after actions", info)
        print(tag, "console:", msgs)
        b.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for w in [int(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]] or [1440, 390]:
        run(w, f"w{w}")
```

```
I've built `interactive.html` in the paper folder. It's a single self-contained file of 1.3 MB with no external scripts, fonts or network calls, and every chart is drawn from eight embedded JSON blocks that a script extracted from the run's output files. I operated every control in headless Chromium at 390, 1280 and 1440 px: no console errors, no sideways scroll, no overlapping chart labels, and tapping a term or chart mark keeps its definition open.

What's on the page, top to bottom:
- **The finding:** a forest plot you can switch between OPEN<sub>home</sub> and NOVCHURN<sub>home</sub> and across control rungs R0, R2 and R3. Each group of concepts shows a grey band for what shuffled outcomes produce. The default view shows the paper's +0.069 [+0.038, +0.100], I² = 0, 6/6 positive, with the development set's +0.109 (1.58×) plotted separately.
- **How it works:** a six-stage stepper that follows the graphics processing unit (GPU) concept through the method using its recorded values. At stage 4 the page recomputes the index in the browser, and it matches the recorded 0.570. Paper figures 1 and 4 sit below with their own captions.
- **Explore the evidence:**
  - A concept browser over 7,748 concepts with search, filter and sort. The detail panel shows the six inputs, the index value, and the popularity-baseline (B5) forecast next to the B5+OPEN forecast and the observed breadth.
  - A chart of breadth minus the B5 forecast for each fifth of OPEN<sub>home</sub>.
  - A forest plot of the entry-model coefficient d₀ by group.
  - An entry browser that lists every candidate field in one concept-year, with probabilities from the baseline model (R2) and the retained-frontier model (R3).
- **Try it:** a live calculator that computes OPEN<sub>home</sub> from its six components, and a slider that recomputes the top-k hit rate over all 14,410 held-out entry events.
- **Where it fails:** the failed pre-registered tests (the volume-matched contrast, the proximity reversal, the dose response that isn't monotone), the noise-control results for NOVCHURN, a table of concepts where openness points the wrong way (with buttons that load them in the browser), and the paper's limitations.

Things you should know:
- **Two d₀ values in the paper disagree.** The table gives the development-set d₀ as 0.228 [0.164, 0.291], but the figure, and the file it comes from, give 0.246 [0.222, 0.271]. The page uses the figure's value. The held-out intervals also follow the figure's bootstrap values, for example Physical Sciences [0.074, 0.219] where the table says [0.078, 0.219].
- **One paper figure isn't reproduced.** The paper says Life & Environment has the weakest OPEN signal (+0.042), but none of the files I read gives that number, so the page doesn't state it.
- **Browser data sample:** the entry browser holds a seeded sample of 30 risk sets per group, and the page says so. The top-k view uses every event.
- **Other edits:** in `index.html` I added only the "Explore the interactive demo" link, in the hero and the footer. I also added one line to `README.md` so its file list includes the new page. The manifest needed no change, and my scratch scripts and screenshots stayed in the session scratchpad, outside the published folder.
```
